title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies glioblastoma cell subsets that stratify survival
summary: The RAPID unsupervised algorithm, applied to mass cytometry data from 28 glioblastomas (about 2 million cells), found cell populations that independently and continuously stratified survival. The findings were confirmed by immunohistochemistry in a larger cohort of 73 patients, and the method also rediscovered known risk-stratifying cells in published blood-cancer data. The pilot cohort is small.
ai_technology: RAPID (Risk Assessment Population IDentification) unsupervised machine-learning algorithm
organization: Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA; Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Nashville, USA

evidence.unknown: Clinical utility and performance in larger prospective cohorts; full text not reviewed.
